calls.reason: The only firm-level evidence is Block. Management credits AI, and ABC's interviews show workers disagree about AI's role and point to overhiring and investor incentives. Neither proves real AI displacement or that every such layoff came from shareholder anger and publicity.

No packet source measures how much non-AI work ran on AI data centers. An FP64 finite-element paper shows a real scientific use, and Civo says AI-oriented GPUs often suit such work poorly. That is too thin to settle 'very little else'.

Photoroom trained its own model and planned to spend funding on GPUs, images and staff, so not every penny goes to Anthropic and OpenAI. Midjourney's founder also said it was profitable. Both cut against 'every AI startup'.

The Agentless paper reports a repeatable average cost per task, which cuts against the cost half. But nothing in the packet addresses measuring ROI, his main point, and the Kapoor paper confirms real standardization problems.

SemiAnalysis's independent benchmarks show Blackwell giving far more tokens per dollar than Hopper, which undercuts the premise. But the claim is hedged ('don't appear', 'heavily suggests') and its business-model conclusion has no test.

NVIDIA's write-up of the SemiAnalysis benchmarks shows GB200 serving tokens far cheaper than H200 at matched speed. Cognition's Rubin test reported lower cost per session. Both point against the unhedged claim, though the sources are vendor-published.
